title: Grateful Dead Live at Utica Memorial Auditorium on 1973-03-21
lineage: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat (Sony D8) -> M-Audio DIO 2448 -> Cool Edit Pro v1.2 -> CD -> EAC -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with a few hum and vocal clipping issues captures an underrated 1973 show featuring stellar Here Comes Sunshine, Dark Star, China>Rider and a killer Bertha opener.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised for its jazzy, flowing vibe and standout jams—especially the Dark Star, Here Comes Sunshine, and the China > Rider sequence—while the soundboard source delivers generally good clarity despite occasional hum, vocal oversaturation and a missing intro to Bertha. Overall the show is considered a hidden gem of the spring ’73 tour.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4‑5 stars, highlighting excellent musical moments and deeming the recording an improvement over earlier tapes; only minor technical flaws are noted.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear mix with a faint hum and occasional vocal oversaturation/clipping; some listeners note the first few seconds of Bertha missing, but overall it is an upgrade over previous circulating tapes.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows with a high‑energy opener (Bertha), a jazzy first set, and a second‑set jam suite that builds into extended improvisations; audience interaction is well captured, adding to the live feel.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for beautiful playing on Here Comes Sunshine, harmonizing on Me and Bobby McGee, and an early Slipknot‑style riff during Take a Step Back.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for witty banter about not playing St. Stephen any more; no specific musical critique.
band_member_comments.Bob: Described as delivering some of his most beautiful playing, especially on Here Comes Sunshine, with a louder mix that brings out his guitar work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s keyboard work is highlighted for the subtle Slipknot riff doodle during Take a Step Back and overall solid support throughout the jams.
